result.title: Rate-distortion Assessment for Hierarchical Content Summarization
result.summary: Powerful generative models including large language and vision models have demonstrated success across a wide range of content generation, editing and manipulation tasks via end-to-end prompt-based generation. However, current assessment of the quality of generative content manipulation remains subjective, limiting scientific understanding of model capabilities. Inspired by rate-distortion theory from Shannon information compression theory, in this work we formalize hierarchical content summarization as an information encoding problem. We design a principled framework to extract the semantic hierarchy of the source content to support quantitative characterization of the rate-distortion trade-off between compression efficiency (rate) against information loss (distortion) during generative content manipulation, which allows us to benchmark various models with respect to performance conditional on rate budget of interest. We demonstrate the use of the framework with empirical experiments on content summarization for long-context question-answering with state-of-the-art large language models, offering new insights into their efficiency and comprehension capabilities. We further demonstrate the use of the semantic hierarchy as guidance for performing effective retrieval augmented generation, showing improved rate-distortion characteristics against current baselines.

AI.brief_summary: 论文将分层内容摘要形式化为信息编码问题，基于率失真理论构建语义层级框架，量化压缩效率与信息损失的权衡，并在长上下文问答与检索增强生成中评估大语言模型。
AI.relevance_reason: 其率失真与语义层级的评估视角可能启发 LVR 对 latent 状态保留任务必要视觉信息、压缩成本与证据筛选的度量，但研究对象是文本摘要，需核查能否迁移到多模态推理状态。
